title: Write the table's lambdas as method references

blocks.text: A method reference is shorthand for a lambda that does nothing but call one existing method. The page's table pairs each reference with its lambda:
Complete `RefTable` so that each factory method returns the function in its row. The tests check what each function does; writing each one as the reference in its row is the practice's aim:
A reference must behave like its lambda on every call, not only the first, and a reference to an instance method has to decide which argument is the receiver.

cases.says: Each function does exactly what its lambda in the table does.
A constructor reference runs the constructor on every call, so each call returns a new list.
In String::compareTo the first argument is the receiver: compare(a, b) is a.compareTo(b).
builder() runs the constructor on each call: every builder is new, holds only its own text, and null is refused as new StringBuilder(null) refuses it.

concepts: The :: operator names a method without calling it; the call happens each time the interface method runs.
Every method reference can be rewritten as the lambda that calls the same method with the same arguments.
